marks.gloss_en: מי גרע ספר תורה מעצמות? -- is a Torah scroll inferior to bones? what may not be done to bones surely may not be done to a Torah scroll
פשיטא! מי גרע ספר תורה מעצמות? -- that would be obvious: a Torah scroll is no less than bones, so the baraita would be teaching nothing
(entertained) the comparison refers to the first clause: a Torah scroll, like bones, may not be ridden on
one who carries bones from place to place may not put them in a saddlebag, set them on a donkey's back and ride on them
whoever sees the dead and does not escort him transgresses on account of 'he who mocks the poor blasphemes his Maker' (Prov 17:5)
one who watches the dead, even if it is not his own dead, is exempt from the Shema, from prayer, from tefillin, and from all the mitzvot said in the Torah
what is between them? Ravina: whether one is concerned about mice is between them
ומי ידעי כולי האי? והא כתיב והמתים אינם יודעים מאומה -- do the dead know so much, that they could feel mocked? (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind names the והא כתיב verse-contradiction)

אם קרית לא שנית, אם שנית לא שלשת, אם שלשת לא פירשו לך -- 'the living know that they will die' are the righteous, called living even in death (18a.14), and 'the dead know nothing' are the wicked, called dead even in life (18b.3); the verse does not speak of the righteous dead (= p_hachayim_hem_tzaddikim, p_hametim_hem_reshaim)
but it is written: 'and the dead know nothing' (Eccl 9:5)
lift it [the trailing tekhelet], so that they [the dead] do not say: tomorrow they come to us, and now they mock us
and (the baraita:) he is exempt from Shema, prayer, tefillin, and all mitzvot of the Torah
the practical difference between the tanna kama and RSbG is marital relations
apply the baraita's exemption clause to the one who turns his face and eats -- the dead IS before him
construal: his own dead -- exempt; one merely watching a corpse -- obligated
the watcher of a corpse, though it is not his dead, is exempt from Shema, prayer, tefillin, and all mitzvot
construal: his dead or watching -- exempt; one walking in a graveyard -- obligated
there, within four cubits of the dead it is forbidden; beyond four cubits one is obligated
